look_here_first: FERN GRASS / CATAPODIUM RIGIDUM — small INTRODUCED, cool-season ANNUAL, generally only about 2–30 cm. The short terminal flowering cluster (often 1–8 cm) looks like a tiny rigid GREEN FERN: numerous stiff nearly straight little ANGULAR / 3-ANGLED branches, with separate oblong, many-flowered SPIKELETS tightly appressed nearly to their bases, giving a one-sided or little ladder/comb appearance. Confirm the minute 0.5–1.5 mm pedicels and one individual 4–7 mm spikelet with about 3–10 fertile FLORETS at 10–20×; the lower and upper glumes are relatively short (~1.5–2.2 mm), and the ~2–2.5 mm fertile lemmas are blunt and five-nerved. At the true leaf collar check the BLUNT, 1–3 mm MEMBRANOUS ligule without a hair fringe. The archived overview photo demonstrates the fernlike arrangement but does not prove angular stem cross section, spikelet floret count, glume veins, lemmas or ligule.

best_field_traits: Small cool-season fibrous-rooted annual often only ~2–30 cm, typically in dry compacted disturbed gravelly/sandy ground; INTRODUCED, native metrics excluded unchanged.
Terminal narrow panicle typically ~1–8 cm, open or sometimes contracted, resembling little green FERN COMBS: branches relatively straight, STIFF and three-angled in cross-section.
Spikelets may appear in dense single-sided ranks along simple short branches, many arising nearly to the axis; not separate airy drooping branchlets as in Poa annua.
Individual spikelet oblong and laterally compressed, mostly ~4–7 mm with ~3–10 fertile florets inside; supported by Kew GrassBase. A floret ≠ a spikelet; don't count branches.
Each spikelet commonly has a very short stout pedicel ~0.5–1.5 mm; true glumes relatively short ~1.5–2.2 mm, unequal, and lemma ~2–2.5 mm with obtuse/blunt tip, five-veined (magnification required).
Blade relatively short, flat or inrolled; the TRUE LIGULE is a BLUNT, ~1–3 mm thin membranous projection, NOT a fringe of hairs.
Other labels Desmazeria rigida, Scleropoa rigida reflect historical treatments of the same species; do not confuse with a new accepted genus card.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: WHOLE ROOTED ANNUAL: fibrous roots and all 2–30 cm plant, including blade tips and uncut 1–8 cm fernlike flowering head, with ruler.
PANICLE AXIS 10–20×: photograph its stiff THREE-ANGLED / angular main stalk and straight simple branches with scale, showing spikelets close to branch bases.
PEDICEL & SPIKELET 10–20×: one intact 4–7 mm compressed oblong spikelet on a short 0.5–1.5 mm wedge-shaped pedicel and its branch point, with mm scale.
ONE DISSECTED SPIKELET 20×: separate two short unequal glumes from the ~3–10 fertile florets INSIDE spikelet; show a blunt 2–2.5 mm lemma and flower attachment.
LIGULE 10–20×: fold back blade and show true BLUNT 1–3 mm MEMBRANE at sheath junction, not just pubescence or its underside.

SAME-SCALE COMPARE: Poa annua open loose triangular seedhead and boat-shaped leaf apex; Eragrostis cilianensis true ciliate/hair ligule and glandular branches/rachilla; preserve each true species label.
crew_field_check: FERN GRASS / CATAPODIUM RIGIDUM — small INTRODUCED, cool-season ANNUAL, generally only about 2–30 cm. The short terminal flowering cluster (often 1–8 cm) looks like a tiny rigid GREEN FERN: numerous stiff nearly straight little ANGULAR / 3-ANGLED branches, with separate oblong, many-flowered SPIKELETS tightly appressed nearly to their bases, giving a one-sided or little ladder/comb appearance. Confirm the minute 0.5–1.5 mm pedicels and one individual 4–7 mm spikelet with about 3–10 fertile FLORETS at 10–20×; the lower and upper glumes are relatively short (~1.5–2.2 mm), and the ~2–2.5 mm fertile lemmas are blunt and five-nerved. At the true leaf collar check the BLUNT, 1–3 mm MEMBRANOUS ligule without a hair fringe. The archived overview photo demonstrates the fernlike arrangement but does not prove angular stem cross section, spikelet floret count, glume veins, lemmas or ligule.

ANNUAL BLUEGRASS / Poa annua: also small and introduced, but its soft open, loose, usually triangular seedhead has more separated/arching branched spikelets and generally BOAT-PROW tips on the blades; Poa has a membranous ligule too, so membrane alone cannot split them. CATAPODIUM has stiff straight/angular branches with short-pedicelled small oblong spikelets packed close along one side, often a tight fernlike silhouette. STINKGRASS / Eragrostis cilianensis: often a larger ascending annual with abundant 5–60-floret spikelets, glandular wartlike spots on branchlets/keels, and a TRUE HAIR-FRINGE ligule; Catapodium's true ligule is a BLUNT, smooth-edged MEMBRANE. Both can be short and have multi-flowered spikelets, so dissect mature florets and check 1–3 mm collar under 10–20×; DO NOT separate by 'many flowers' alone. Other fernlike grasses such as small Poa/Eragrostis or Scleropoa need exact glumes/lemma and branch cross sections. Old DESMAZERIA RIGIDA and SCLEROPOA RIGIDA are synonyms in some treatments, not separate installed species.

Photo confidence: current actual Catapodium image proves small fernlike stiff/closely attached branches only. Get connected rooted plant, angular main axis cross-section, 4–7 mm measured multi-floret spikelet, and true 1–3 mm membrane ligule before treating a difficult small-grass photo as definitive.

visual_comparison.title: Fern grass — three verified real photos: rigid fernlike head versus softer bluegrass and stinkgrass
visual_comparison.subtitle: Three same-species photos physically stored and presented (habit and two source-labelled ligule close-ups) plus two other-species comparisons. Diagnostic membrane boundaries, millimeter scale, spikelet/lemma macros still require verification.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: FERN GRASS: SHORT ANNUAL + STIFF 3-ANGLED FERN-COMB PANICLE + SHORT PEDICELS + 4–7 mm MULTI-FLORET spikelets + BLUNT 1–3 mm MEMBRANOUS LIGULE. Not Poa's soft open triangle; not Eragrostis cilianensis's glandular head and HAIR ligule.

items.label: 2 · ANNUAL BLUEGRASS — OTHER species, soft open panicle
items.image_role: Physically installed and viewed true Poa annua habit reference; DIFFERENT species comparison only, not a fern grass photo.
items.caption: This is ANNUAL BLUEGRASS, not Catapodium. Harry Rose's photo has soft, loose, widely spreading seedhead branches rather than the many closely attached stiff angular little fern-combs of Catapodium. Poa blades may terminate in a boat-prow tip, but no single leaf-tip macro or ligule measurement is independently certified here.
items.why_it_matters: Tiny annual grasses can both have branching multi-flowered heads; the open/loose Poa structure and its folded boat-ended leaf are good first separations.
items.creator: Harry Rose (Macleay Grass Man)
items.photo_status: 2026-10-22 source Poa annua original photo visually inspected from existing GitHub local JPEG; credited other-species comparison, no anatomy arrows.

items.label: 3 · STINKGRASS — OTHER species, not the same membrane collar
items.image_role: Physically installed and viewed bona fide Eragrostis cilianensis habit photo; different species for annual thin-branch comparison only.
items.caption: This is STINKGRASS (Eragrostis cilianensis), not fern grass. The genuine archived photo shows multiple small grain-bearing panicles on longer thin stalks. Confirm Eragrostis by the TRUE HAIR-FRINGE ligule and often wartlike glands on panicle branches and spikelet keels, not an imagined microscopic character from this habit photo; Catapodium has a blunt membrane ligule and stiff 3-angled short branches.
items.why_it_matters: Eragrostis and Catapodium have multi-flowered spikelets, so a close-up of the actual collar and mature lemma and tiny glands—not floret count alone—is the safe split.
items.creator: sonoresmore
items.photo_status: 2026-10-22 actual Eragrostis source image viewed directly in GitHub, source-declared CC0 metadata unchanged; comparison not a new species admission and no gland arrows.
